root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Scorpion-Horus Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. Nc3 d5 3. d3 dxe4 4. Bg5

overview: Against the 2.Nc3 Caro-Kann White plays 3.d3 dxe4 4.Bg5, developing with a lead in development and a pin on the knight rather than recapturing the pawn at once. Black is a pawn up and can hold it with ...Qb6 or ...f6-type moves. It is a surprise line with little theory.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Bg5, Nxe4 or dxe4 and Qd2
Look for tactics on f7 and the d-file

black_ideas.idea: Keep the pawn with accurate defence and development
Exchange queens or neutralise Bg5 with ...Nf6 and ...Qb6

typical_structures.structure: Caro-Kann with Black pawn on e4 and white d3

character.notes: White's pawn sacrifice leads to early tactics.

gambit.notes: Black has taken e4 and White has not yet regained it; Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Black can hold the pawn, so White's compensation is thin.

structure.notes: Semi-open centre; the c6-d5 pawn pair has been traded.

level.notes: Dubious so not Beginner; concrete play but not much to learn.

sublines_that_differ.name: Normal recapture
sublines_that_differ.how: Not a gambit; White gets a quiet position after queen exchange.

character.reason: The gambit gives early tactics, though Black can steer towards a quiet position.

gambit.reason: White offers e4 with 3.d3 and 4.Bg5 and Black can keep the pawn.

soundness.reason: Black can keep the pawn with accurate development.

structure.reason: The centre opens with ...dxe4, giving the structure a Caro-Kann semi-open look.

approach.reason: Strong players rarely play this against the Caro-Kann.

level.reason: Dubious so not Beginner; Black must know the key defensive resources.

plans.reason: White hopes the lead in development outweighs the pawn.
